title: PowerPoint on Mac: reference an attached deck's style when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: the licensing model reports mixed entitlement without documentation establishing that model for this feature. The roadmap facts, user workflow and licence-assignment controls are supported; the shortened licence-check path also needs a small correction.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature's release-notes entry describes no new sign-in, permission, connector or autonomous action.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model
claims.claim: The attached-deck style feature has a mixed licensing model.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode attach presentation theme styles licensing requirements credit meter Basic Premium; PowerPoint Copilot style licensing. Opened Copilot overview and release-notes: they describe product tiers, not a mixed entitlement model for this feature.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "included" for a new option inside the existing licensed product, retaining the notes' distinction between Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) and the narrow uncertainty about this feature's tier. The product overview lists presentation creation and editing among existing in-app capabilities: https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-overview.

claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: User licence assignments are managed in Microsoft 365 admin center at Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PowerShell assigns a user licence with Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @().
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.where: summary; Governance controls; Open questions: admin setting

claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot reference attached deck style admin policy disable feature Graph PowerShell; PowerPoint Agent Mode admin control. Opened release-notes and configure-copilot-admin-center; results cover other agents or general Copilot controls, not this feature's own switch.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: The licence-check route is Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > Licenses and Apps.

claims.fix: In Governance guidance's licence-check bullet, replace the shortened parenthetical path with "Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses". Selecting the user is a scope-selection step omitted from the otherwise correct path; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/assign-licenses-to-users documents it.
